translation.canonical_title: Modern feminism flirts with misandry (hatred of men)
translation.displayed_title: Modern feminism flirts with misandry (hatred of men)
translation.summary:
On August 19, 2020, the pamphlet "I Hate Men" was quietly released in a print run of 450 copies. Its author, Pauline Harmange, 25, married and relatively unknown, ran a blog and described herself as a feminist. The book received unexpected media coverage after Ralph Zumély, an adviser on gender equality, threatened to have it banned. The enthusiasm matched the reach of its provocative title. To meet demand, the essay was republished by Seuil in September 2020 and sold like hotcakes. The author openly identifies as a misandrist and intends to denounce men as a social group that harms women.
It recalls openly misandrist writings from the twentieth century that have since been forgotten, including Valerie Solanas's famous 1967 SCUM Manifesto (Solanas shot Andy Warhol), as well as essayists such as Natalie Clifford Barney and Mireille Havet.

'''#menaretrash'''
Nor should the digital sphere be forgotten: it offers vast territory for hatred. The hashtag #menaretrash ("men are trash") emerged in South Africa in 2016. After a series of femicides, it gained renewed attention in 2017 and then spread across social media worldwide. Although most tweets and other posts using it denounced abuse, some saw the hashtag as sweeping and stigmatizing, if not hateful. Those more hostile to it revived the debate over cancel culture and accused the hashtag of serving as a tool for trial by social media, independently of legal procedures and at the risk of overriding them.

The media attention and some people's concern about this overt misandry raise questions: revenge? Communitarianism? Radical feminism? The subject will continue to inflame people of both sexes.

Je vois dans la misandrie une porte de sortie. Une manière d'exister en dehors du passage clouté, une manière de dire non à chaque respiration. Détester les hommes, en tant que groupe social et souvent en tant qu'individus aussi, m'apporte beaucoup de joie – et pas seulement parce que je suis une vieille sorcière folle à chats.
Si on devenait toutes misandres, on pourrait former une grande et belle sarabande. On se rendrait compte (et ce serait peut-être un peu douloureux au début) qu'on n'a vraiment pas besoin des hommes. On pourrait, je crois, libérer un pouvoir insoupçonné : celui, en planant très loin au-dessus du regard des hommes et des exigences masculines, de nous révéler à nous-mêmes

citations.translated_citation:
I see misandry as a way out. A way to exist outside the marked crossing, a way to say no with every breath. Hating men, as a social group and often as individuals too, brings me a great deal of joy—and not only because I am a crazy old cat lady.
If we all became misandrists, we could form one great, beautiful saraband. We would realize (and it might hurt a little at first) that we truly do not need men. I believe we could unleash an unsuspected power: that of revealing ourselves to ourselves by soaring far above men's gaze and male demands.

Vivre dans cette société, c’est au mieux y mourir d’ennui. Rien dans cette société ne concerne les femmes. Alors, à toutes celles qui ont un brin de civisme, le sens des responsabilités et celui de la rigolade, il ne reste qu’à renverser le gouvernement, en finir avec l’argent, instaurer l’automation à tous les niveaux et supprimer le sexe masculin.
Le mâle est un accident biologique ; le gène Y (mâle) n’est qu’un gène X (femelle) incomplet, une série incomplète de chromosomes. En d’autres termes, l’homme est une femme manquée, une fausse couche ambulante, un avorton congénital.
Les hommes sont des Midas d’un genre spécial : tout ce qu’ils touchent se change en merde.
Ce qui met l’homme en joie – dans la mesure où cette créature sinistre et constipée est capable d’éprouver de la joie – c’est de dénoncer les autres.

citations.translated_citation:
Living in this society means, at best, dying of boredom. Nothing in this society concerns women. Therefore, all those with a shred of civic spirit, a sense of responsibility and a sense of humor have no option but to overthrow the government, abolish money, institute complete automation and eliminate the male sex.
The male is a biological accident; the Y (male) gene is merely an incomplete X (female) gene, an incomplete set of chromosomes. In other words, man is a failed woman, a walking miscarriage, a congenital runt.
Men are a special kind of Midas: everything they touch turns to shit.
What delights a man—insofar as this sinister, constipated creature is capable of feeling delight—is informing on others.

source_parameters.value: (…) J’ai en moi la haine de l’homme (…). Tout en eux me semble grossier et ridicule, j’ai la haine de leur corps, de leur chair, de leur sexe, de leur désir. Ils sont pour moi d’infâmes faiseurs d’enfants, blesseurs de rêve, ennemis et bourreaux de nos tendresse et de nos féminités. J’ai la haine de l’homme ! (…) Les hommes, quelle cochonnerie.

citations.translated_citation: (…) I harbor hatred for men (…). Everything about them seems coarse and ridiculous to me; I hate their bodies, their flesh, their sex, their desire. To me they are vile child-makers, destroyers of dreams, enemies and tormentors of our tenderness and our femininity. I hate men! (…) Men—what filth.
